scope_note: metaspike_score_v0 measures relative attention anomaly and recent momentum from a single source (Wikimedia pageviews, daily). It is not a complete measure of creator demand or supply.

terms.name: significance
terms.rationale: How unusual the latest day is against the game's own day-to-day variability. A robust z of 3.5 is the conventional outlier threshold and earns half credit; twice that saturates.

terms.name: magnitude
terms.rationale: How far the 3-day average sits above the game's own 28-day median, in doublings because attention grows multiplicatively. 8x normal saturates.

terms.name: anomaly
terms.rationale: Geometric mean, so an anomaly must be BOTH statistically unusual and large. Significance alone over-rewards tiny moves in very stable series; magnitude alone over-rewards noise in small, volatile ones.

terms.name: momentum
terms.rationale: Whether attention is still accelerating: the 3-day average against the preceding 3 days. Doubling saturates. Undefined velocity counts as 0.

terms.name: score
terms.rationale: Anomaly is the primary signal and momentum the secondary one. The weights are stated priors, not fitted values. Declines clamp to 0: v0 scores upward attention only.

terms.name: source_ceiling
terms.rationale: Independent corroboration is the main driver of confidence. With one source the ceiling is 0.60, so confidence can never exceed 60.

terms.name: freshness
terms.rationale: Data that lags the expected latest day says less about 'right now'.

terms.name: history
terms.rationale: A short history gives a weaker picture of what is normal for the game.

terms.name: completeness
terms.rationale: Missing days inside the history weaken every statistic built on it.

terms.name: samples
terms.rationale: Whether the windows the score depends on were actually fully populated.

terms.name: confidence
terms.rationale: Multiplicative, so any single weakness lowers confidence and none can be averaged away by the others.

event_heat.scope_note: Event Heat is internal and uncalibrated (event_heat_rules_v1). It is reported beside metaspike_score_v0 and is not part of it. Unavailable means no source has looked at a game's events recently; it never means zero.

terms.name: strength, before the start
terms.formula: pre_event_peak * (1 - days_to_start / ramp_days), inside the ramp; else 0
terms.rationale: Anticipation builds as a dated event approaches. Outside the ramp an event is scheduled and has no strength yet.

terms.name: strength, while running
terms.rationale: The start is the peak. Novelty then halves every half-life, but an event that is still running never falls below its floor.

terms.name: strength, after the end
terms.rationale: Influence fades from where it stood when the event ended and stops counting once the window has passed.

terms.name: contribution
terms.rationale: A type's importance is also the most one event of it can contribute.

terms.name: event_heat
terms.formula: scale * (1 - product(1 - contribution)), over the largest max_contributing_events contributions
terms.rationale: Each event contributes importance x strength, between 0 and 1. Events of the same type starting on the same UTC day count once, at the larger contribution, so an unmerged duplicate cannot count twice. The max_contributing_events largest contributions c are combined as heat = scale x (1 - product(1 - c)). The result is never below the largest single contribution, never reaches the scale unless one contribution is 1, and adding an event never lowers it.

event_heat.aggregation: Each event contributes importance x strength, between 0 and 1. Events of the same type starting on the same UTC day count once, at the larger contribution, so an unmerged duplicate cannot count twice. The max_contributing_events largest contributions c are combined as heat = scale x (1 - product(1 - c)). The result is never below the largest single contribution, never reaches the scale unless one contribution is 1, and adding an event never lowers it.

availability.name: available, heat 0
availability.formula: a source looked within coverage_max_age_days; no relevant event
availability.rationale: A finding: someone looked and there is nothing.

availability.name: available, heat above 0
availability.formula: a source looked within coverage_max_age_days; relevant events exist
availability.rationale: The events and each one's contribution are listed.

availability.name: unavailable
availability.formula: no source has looked, or the last look is older than coverage_max_age_days
availability.rationale: Not knowing is never reported as zero. The heat is null and the reason is given.

parameters.name: scale
parameters.rationale: The same 0 to 100 scale as the score and confidence, so the three read alike. It is a different quantity and is not added to either.

parameters.name: max_contributing_events
parameters.rationale: A game is rarely about more than a few things at once. Counting only the three strongest stops a pile of small events from looking like one large one.

parameters.name: coverage_max_age_days
parameters.rationale: Dates move. If no source has looked at a game's events for two weeks, what is known may be out of date, and heat is reported as unavailable, never as zero.

parameters.name: horizon_days
parameters.rationale: A month is as far ahead as a dated announcement is useful for planning content, and the longest ramp any type has.

parameters.name: radar_windows_hours
parameters.rationale: The next day, the next week and the next month: what can still be prepared for today, this week, and with planning.

types.label: Release
types.rationale: The largest moment a game has. Anticipation builds for a month, the day itself is the peak, and interest halves about weekly for a month after.

types.label: Expansion
types.rationale: A second launch for an existing audience: nearly as large as a release, with a shorter build-up and tail.

types.label: Platform release
types.rationale: A launch for a new audience only. Real, but smaller than the original.

types.label: New season
types.rationale: A season's start is the event; the season then runs for weeks. Strength halves every five days and holds at a low floor until the season ends.

types.label: Wipe
types.rationale: A reset everyone plays through at once. Sharp, anticipated a few days ahead, and largely over within two weeks.

types.label: Major update
types.rationale: Changes what there is to say about a game. Usually dated a few days ahead; interest fades within about ten days.

types.label: DLC
types.rationale: New content smaller than an expansion.

types.label: Expedition
types.rationale: A time-limited community event that runs for weeks, strongest at its start.

types.label: In-game event
types.rationale: A live moment inside the game. Short, so it stays near full strength while it runs and fades within days.

types.label: Beta
types.rationale: First hands-on access for a wide audience, for a limited time.

types.label: Playtest
types.rationale: Limited access, smaller than a beta.

types.label: Free weekend
types.rationale: A few days in which anyone can play. It matters while it lasts and little after.

types.label: Showcase
types.rationale: A dated presentation. Speculation builds for a week and the reaction is spent within days.

types.label: Trailer
types.rationale: Often a surprise, so there is little build-up. Reaction content has a short life.

types.label: Minor update
types.rationale: Routine maintenance. Recorded, and deliberately worth little: three of them together stay well under one major patch.

limitations: Internal and uncalibrated: every value is an engineering prior, not fitted to outcomes and not backtested.
No event source is collected yet. Until one is, event intelligence is unavailable for every game.
Event Heat is not part of metaspike_score_v0 and does not affect any rank.

Events are matched by exact rules only. Two reports of one event that share no id, reference or title stay separate; heat counts one event per type and start day so that such a duplicate cannot count twice.
A source without native event ids that moves a date is seen as reporting a new event.
Importance is per type, not per game: a small game's release and a large game's are treated alike.
All days are UTC. An event known only to the day starts at 00:00 UTC.

features.principle: Each game is compared against its own recent normal, never against other games' raw popularity. All windows are anchored on t, the latest observed day; missing days are excluded from every window, never counted as zero.

definitions.name: latest_views
definitions.definition: x[t]: pageviews on t, the latest day with an observation.
definitions.valid_when: at least one observed day in the window

definitions.name: avg_3d
definitions.definition: Mean of observed days in [t-2, t].

definitions.name: avg_7d
definitions.definition: Mean of observed days in [t-6, t].

definitions.name: baseline_mean_28d / baseline_std_28d
definitions.definition: Rolling mean and sample standard deviation (n-1) of observed days in the baseline window [t-34, t-7].

definitions.name: baseline_median_28d / baseline_mad_28d
definitions.definition: Median m of the baseline window, and MAD = median(|x_i - m|) over the same days. The median is the game's 'normal' level; it is unaffected by old spikes.

definitions.name: velocity_ratio / velocity_pct
definitions.definition: velocity_ratio = avg_3d / prior_avg_3d, where prior_avg_3d is the mean of observed days in [t-5, t-3]; velocity_pct = (velocity_ratio - 1) * 100.
definitions.valid_when: both 3-day windows have >= 2 observed days and prior_avg_3d > 0

definitions.name: consecutive_rising_days
definitions.definition: Number of consecutive day-over-day increases ending at t. A missing day ends the run.
definitions.valid_when: always (0 when there is no run)

definitions.name: robust_z_score
definitions.definition: (x[t] - baseline_median_28d) / s, with s = 1.4826 * MAD. If MAD is 0, s = 1.2533 * mean(|x_i - m|) instead (robust_scale_method = 'mean_ad'). Unlike z_score it is not inflated or masked by earlier outliers.

definitions.name: history_percentile
definitions.definition: Mid-rank percentile of x[t] among all observed days before t in the fetched window: 100 * (count(x_i < x[t]) + 0.5 * count(x_i = x[t])) / n.

definitions.name: staleness_days
definitions.definition: Days by which t trails the latest day the source was due to have published, given its expected publication lag. Never negative.
definitions.valid_when: at least one observed day in the window

definitions.name: missing_days
definitions.definition: Days with no observation between the first observed day and t.

explanations: Deterministic templates rendered from computed features. A sentence appears only when its backing feature crosses a fixed threshold. No language model.

metrics.description: Human (non-bot) views of the page that represents the game.

sources.description: Daily human (non-bot) pageviews of the game's English Wikipedia article, all access methods, from the Wikimedia Analytics API.

rate_limit.note: 200 requests/minute for unauthenticated clients with a compliant User-Agent. The Analytics API asks clients to wait for each request to finish before sending another, hence a concurrency of 1.

display.note: CC0 data carries no display condition. Wikimedia marks must not be used in a way that implies endorsement.

field_rules.note: Aggregate daily counts; no personal data.

policy.notes: API data is published under CC0 1.0. Use is subject to the Wikimedia Terms of Use: a descriptive User-Agent with contact information is mandatory, requests must be made one at a time, and clients that endanger service stability may be blocked. No publication schedule is documented for daily data: one hour after a day ended it was not yet available, so a 24-hour lag is allowed for until measured.

limitations: Single source: only Wikimedia pageviews are collected, so nothing is corroborated and confidence is capped at 60.
Wikipedia readership is a proxy for general public attention. It is not player counts, viewership, search demand or creator supply.
Daily granularity in UTC. The newest point is the last complete day, typically 1 day old.
English Wikipedia only, so attention from non-English audiences is under-represented.
Views of redirect titles are counted separately by the source and are not included.
A game with no article of its own (for example FiveM) has no coverage and is unranked.
A day the source omits is treated as missing, not as zero views.
No event detection yet: the score reports that attention moved, not what caused it.
Weekly seasonality is not modelled; the 28-day baseline spans four whole weeks to limit, but not remove, its effect.
Score weights and saturation points are stated priors, not values fitted to outcomes.
The score rewards upward attention only; declines score 0 rather than negative.
